## Alternative solution

```{r}
#| label: Load data bis
#| eval: false
# Create the data directory programmatically
dir.create(path = "data")

# Retrieve the data directly
diabetes_data <- read_csv(file = "https://hbiostat.org/data/repo/diabetes.csv")

# Write the data to disk
write_csv(x = diabetes_data,
          file = "data/diabetes.csv")
```

Q1: 403 observations, 19 variables Q2: 3 rules: - Each observation has its own row (yes) - Each variable has its own column (yes) - Each value has its own cell (yes) Q3: It is the column type (chr stands for character, dbl for double)

```{r}
#| label: Task 1

diabetes_data <- diabetes_data |>
  mutate(height = round(height * 2.54, 1),
         weight = round(weight * 0.453592, 1),
         waist  = round(waist * 2.54, 1),
         hip    = round(hip * 2.54, 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: Question 4

diabetes_data |>
  filter(weight<100) |>
  count()
```

diabetes_data |>

Q15: 4 columns start with letter b

```{r}
#| label: Task 5

diabetes_data <- diabetes_data |> 
  mutate(BMI_class = case_when(
    BMI < 25 ~ "Normal weight",
    25 <= BMI & BMI < 30 ~ "Overweight",
    30 <= BMI & BMI < 35 ~ "Obesity class I",
    35 <= BMI & BMI < 40 ~ "Obesity class II",
    BMI >= 40 ~ "Obesity class III"))

diabetes_data <- diabetes_data |>
  mutate(BMI_class = factor(BMI_class,
                            levels =  c("Normal weight", "Overweight",
                                        "Obesity class I", "Obesity class II",
                                        "Obesity class III")))
```

```{r}
#| label: Task 6

ggplot(data = diabetes_data,
       mapping = aes(x = hdl,
                     y = BMI_class)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

Q17: Looks like there is a correlation between hdl and obesity

```{r}
#| label: Task 7

diabetes_data <- diabetes_data |>
  mutate(BFP = 1.39 * BMI + 0.16 * age - 10.34 * ifelse(gender == "female", 0, 1) - 9)
```

```{r}
#| label: Task 8
#| 
diabetes_data <- diabetes_data |>
  mutate(WHR = waist / hip)
```

```{r}
#| label: Question 18

p1 <- ggplot(data = diabetes_data,
       mapping = aes(x = BFP,
                     y = BMI)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm')

p2 <- ggplot(data = diabetes_data,
       mapping = aes(x = WHR,
                     y = BMI)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm')

p1 + p2
```

```{r}
#| label: Question 18 bis

cor(diabetes_data$BFP, diabetes_data$BMI, use = "complete.obs")
cor(diabetes_data$WHR, diabetes_data$BMI, use = "complete.obs")
```

Considering the graph with linear regressions and the correlation coefficients, we can tell that there is almost no correlation between BMI and WHR, while there is a strong one between BDF and BMI
